items.defectStatement: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an all-groups VIEW-only grant passes the global manage check. This permits operations such as top-level group creation without manage permission.
obligations: Reject VIEW-only grants in the no-argument manage check.
items.notes: The finding overstates the affected endpoints: group-specific update/delete checks use canManage(GroupModel), which already requires MANAGE.

items.defectStatement: JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery requires a resource named group.resource.<groupId>, whereas V2 resources are named with the group ID alone. Consequently, group-restricted user searches and counts exclude authorized members when only V2 resources exist, even if supplied group IDs are correct.
obligations: Allow authorized V2 group members in filtered user searches and counts without requiring legacy resources.
Keep results restricted to authorized group membership and the requested realm.
items.notes: The anchor only returns the set; the defective JPA predicate and its surrounding contract are absent from the frozen input. Correcting resource IDs in #02 does not fix this independent issue.

items.defectStatement: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authorization resource UUIDs instead of resource names, which contain the group IDs. This makes permission lookup miss the group-specific resource and returns identifiers that cannot match user group memberships.
obligations: Evaluate each group's member-view permission using its actual group ID.
Add actual group IDs, rather than authorization resource UUIDs, to the returned set.
Continue accepting VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS and exclude groups whose check fails.
items.notes: Both getId() occurrences must change. The separate legacy JPA resource-name restriction in #04 remains outside this fix.

items.defectStatement: getSubGroups() unconditionally performs a per-group visibility check for every subgroup examined by the listing filter. For V2 all-groups viewers, this repeats authorization evaluation instead of using one global visibility check to bypass those filter checks.
obligations: Compute global group visibility once before filtering.
Skip per-subgroup visibility checks in the filter when global visibility is granted.
Retain per-subgroup filtering when global visibility is denied.
Preserve parent authorization, search parameters, filtering before pagination, and representation mapping.
items.notes: Local classification applies to the finding's getSubGroups regression. The analogous GroupsResource listing requires a separate edit. Representation access calculations may still evaluate permissions; this fix removes repeated visibility-filter checks.
